root_cause.text: `tap_ioctl()` in `drivers/net/tap.c` allocated a stack `struct sockaddr_storage ss` for the `SIOCGIFHWADDR` path without initializing it, and `netif_get_mac_address()` only filled the family and MAC-length portion, so copying `ss` to `ifr_hwaddr` leaked the uninitialized trailing bytes of kernel stack memory to userspace.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `struct sockaddr_storage ss;` to `struct sockaddr_storage ss = {};`, and the commit message states that `netif_get_mac_address()` writes only `sa_family` and `dev->addr_len` bytes, leaving `sa_data[6..13]` uninitialized before `tap_ioctl()` copies 16 bytes to userspace.

intent_record.intent_summary: Zero-initialize the local sockaddr_storage in tap_ioctl() to avoid use of uninitialized stack data.
intent_record.what: In `tap_ioctl()`, the declaration of `struct sockaddr_storage ss` was moved above the `ifr`, `up`, `u`, `sp`, `s`, and `ret` declarations, and it was changed from an uninitialized local variable to a zero-initialized one using `= {}`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, `ss` now starts with all bytes cleared instead of containing indeterminate stack data, which prevents use of uninitialized contents if the structure is partially filled or later inspected before full assignment.

grouping_result.intent: Zero-initialize the local sockaddr_storage in tap_ioctl() to avoid use of uninitialized stack data.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it zero-initializes the local sockaddr_storage in tap_ioctl() to prevent leaking uninitialized stack bytes when copying the hardware address to userspace.

candidates.rationale: This stack variable was allocated without initialization, and later used in the SIOCGIFHWADDR path after only partial filling, leaving trailing bytes uninitialized and leakable to userspace.

vuln_statements.explanation: This local stack allocation was left uninitialized in tap_ioctl(). In the SIOCGIFHWADDR path, only part of it was filled before being copied out, which could leak the remaining uninitialized kernel stack bytes to userspace.

Author: Kees Cook <kees@kernel.org>

    net: core: Convert dev_set_mac_address_user() to use struct sockaddr_storage
    
    Convert callers of dev_set_mac_address_user() to use struct
    sockaddr_storage. Add sanity checks on dev->addr_len usage.
    
    Signed-off-by: Kees Cook <kees@kernel.org>
    Acked-by: Gustavo A. R. Silva <gustavoars@kernel.org>
    Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20250521204619.23
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present in this diff. For the readback path, the code now uses `struct sockaddr_storage ss` and copies only `sizeof(ifr->ifr_hwaddr)` to userspace: `copy_to_user(&ifr->ifr_hwaddr, &ss, sizeof(ifr->ifr_hwaddr))`, which avoids exposing the full uninitialized stack object. This commit also adds a sanity check before setting the MAC address: `if (tap->dev->addr_len > sizeof(ifr->ifr_hwaddr)) ret = -EINVAL; else ret = dev_set_mac_address_user(tap->dev, &ss, NULL);`. Since the specific leak path from copying an uninitialized `struct sockaddr`/`sockaddr_storage` to userspace is no longer shown here, the vulnerable construct is absent and the fix is already present.
